name: Athletics
domain_note: Gross motor under load. GPT selects Power for burst effort, Endurance for sustained effort.
description: Whole-body physical capability under pressure: hauling, climbing, swimming, forced movement, raw grappling. The gross-motor execution side of physicality, distinct from the fine-motor control of Mobility.
examples: Dragging an ally from a collapsing building
Forcing a stuck door open
Swimming against a hard current

name: Mobility
description: Controlled movement, balance, and reactive footwork. Fine-motor body control distinct from Athletics' raw effort. Covers acrobatics, terrain traversal, evasion, riding balance, and recovery from falls.
examples: Rooftop chase across broken tile
Tumbling clear of a collapsing ceiling
Keeping your seat when the horse rears

name: Stealth
description: Remaining unnoticed: quiet movement, concealment, shadowing, infiltration, and exfiltration. The discipline of not being seen, heard, or remembered.
examples: Slipping past guards in a lit corridor
Tailing a target through a market without being made
Finding a hiding place under pressure

name: Skulduggery
description: Precision illicit technique: sleight of hand, lockwork, trap handling, document forgery, disguise prep, sabotage. The technical side of dirty work, distinct from Stealth's remaining unseen.
examples: Picking a pocket in a crowded market
Bypassing a trapped lock
Forging a travel writ

name: Awareness
description: Reading the immediate environment: noticing danger, spotting changes, scanning crowds, detecting ambushes, sensing tension. Active watchfulness in the moment, distinct from Investigation's structured inquiry.
examples: Spotting the assassin in a diplomatic reception
Feeling the room shift before violence breaks out
Catching the tell on a liar

name: Investigation
domain_note: Perception for physical evidence work; Intellect for analytical synthesis and deduction.
description: Structured inquiry: evidence reading, deduction, scene reconstruction, anomaly analysis, interrogation, document examination. The retrospective and analytical counterpart to Awareness's immediate noticing.
examples: Reconstructing a murder from blood spatter
Finding the forgery in a stack of legitimate contracts
Cross-examining a witness

name: Tracking
description: Following movement through the world: spoor reading, passage-time estimation, route inference, quarry habits, urban shadowing at the physical trail level, and counter-tracking.
examples: Dating tracks through a forest floor
Predicting where the fleeing target will emerge
Erasing your own trail through pursuit terrain

name: Survival
description: Living through hostile conditions: shelter, firecraft, weather reading, camp selection, hazard response, navigation, and endurance under field privation. The active discipline of not dying in conditions, distinct from Nature's understanding of living systems.
examples: Building shelter in a freezing storm
Starting a fire with damp wood
Navigating by stars through unfamiliar terrain

name: Nature
description: Understanding living systems: animals, plants, agriculture, ecology. The knowledge of how living things work, distinct from Survival's hostile-conditions response. A botanist has high Nature and zero Survival.
examples: Identifying a poisonous plant on sight
Calming a panicked herd
Diagnosing why an orchard is failing

name: Medicine
description: Diagnosis, treatment, wound care, pharmacology, surgery, and mental care. The medical discipline focused on humanoid bodies and minds. Veterinary work lives under Nature.
examples: Stabilizing a gut wound in the field
Identifying a poison from its symptoms
Treating shock after violence

name: Warfare
domain_note: Will for presence and nerve on the battlefield; Intellect for tactical analysis.
description: Understanding violence: battlefield reading, threat assessment, formation logic, command presence, martial intimidation. The knowing side of combat. A general has Warfare; a gladiator has Combat.
examples: Reading an ambush before it closes
Holding a unit's discipline under artillery
Spotting the weakness in an enemy formation

name: Craft
description: Making and repairing practical things: smithing, carpentry, masonry, leatherwork, textiles, cooking, pottery, maintenance. The trades of physical production.
examples: Forging a blade that holds edge
Repairing a collapsed roof beam
Preparing a feast for a visiting noble

name: Engineering
description: Mechanisms, structures, load paths, siege logic, lockworks, and the material preparation of substrates that can hold magic. More systemic than Craft — engineering is about how and why things hold together.
examples: Designing a working trap
Analyzing bridge failure before collapse
Preparing a stone foundation to receive enchantment

name: Lore
description: Academic and civic memory: history, linguistics, law, religion (as study), politics, genealogy, cartography, economics. The world's accumulated knowledge. Distinct from Arcana's magical theory.
examples: Recalling a century-old treaty clause
Translating an archaic inscription
Tracing a family's hidden lineage

name: Influence
description: Social leverage: persuasion, deception, diplomacy, command, pressure, seduction, etiquette. The full spectrum of shaping other people's behavior.
examples: Talking a guard into letting you pass
Negotiating terms with a hostile faction
Applying pressure to extract a favor

name: Performance
description: Performative expression: singing, instruments, dance, oratory, theatrical work, storytelling. Distinct from Influence — a performance isn't trying to change someone's mind, it's being witnessed.
examples: Holding a tavern rapt with a long ballad
Delivering a funeral oration
Dancing at a high noble's wedding

name: Discipline
description: Self-mastery: focus, courage, resolve, composure, meditation, fear mastery, oath endurance. The inner regulation of attention, emotion, and commitment.
examples: Maintaining concentration during a long ritual
Holding ground against a charging terror
Keeping an oath that costs everything

name: Arcana
description: Non-spell magical understanding: theoretical knowledge, ritual structure analysis, field recognition, enchantment reading, risk assessment. Knowing magic without casting it. Required for identifying what a magical working is, what it does, and how dangerous it might be.
examples: Identifying the field behind an unknown spell
Reading a ward without activating it
Analyzing an enchanted object's function

name: Close Combat
description: Fighting with small, fast, close-range weapons — knives, daggers, throwing blades, brass knuckles, and similar. Distinct from Martial Arts (unarmed), Melee (sword-length weapons), and Martial Grappling (wrestling without weapons).
examples: Trade knife-work in a tavern brawl
Press a dagger into clinch range
Throw a knife at a fleeing target

name: Melee
description: Fighting with one-handed and two-handed sword-length and blunt weapons — swords, clubs, maces, axes, war hammers, and the larger two-handed variants. The standard category of hand-to-hand weapon combat.
examples: Trade blows with a swordsman
Bring a war hammer down on a shield
Swing a greataxe at a charging opponent

name: Reach
description: Fighting with long-shafted weapons that extend reach — spears, pikes, polearms, halberds, war staves. Controls distance and leverage rather than trading hits at arm's length.
examples: Keep foes back with a spear
Hook a rider from the saddle with a halberd
Thrust a pike through a shield wall

name: Ranged
description: Attacking at distance with hand-powered projectile weapons — bows, slings, thrown weapons. Draws on perception and steady hand rather than raw force.
examples: Put an arrow through a gap in cover
Sling stones at pursuers
Loose a Longbough longbow on a moving target

name: Mechanical
description: Operating mechanical projectile weapons — crossbows, blowguns, and similar devices that use stored or channeled mechanical force rather than direct bodily power. Loading, maintaining, and firing is distinct from bow technique.
examples: Reload a heavy crossbow under fire
Aim a light crossbow through cover
Steady a blowgun for a precise dart

name: Unconventional
domain_note: GPT judges per specific weapon; domain may vary by application.
description: Fighting with weapons that do not fit standard melee, reach, ranged, or mechanical categories — nets, chains, whips, improvised or exotic weapons used in non-standard ways. Emphasizes control, restraint, and unconventional application over standard damage output.
examples: Ensnare a target with a thrown net
Use a chain to wrap and pull an opponent's weapon
Snap a whip to disarm or distract

name: Martial Arts
domain_note: Agility for precise technique, Power for force-driven striking.
description: Unarmed fighting — trained striking, kicking, blocking, and hand-to-hand technique without weapons. Distinct from Close Combat (small weapons), Martial Grappling (wrestling), and brawling-as-improvised-violence.
examples: Drop a guard with a trained elbow strike
Block an incoming knife with a forearm
Kick a charging opponent back into cover

name: Armor
domain_note: Endurance for wear and load; Agility for retained mobility.
description: Knowledge of armor types, fitting, maintenance, and operational use across construction styles.
examples: Identify the construction class of an unfamiliar piece of armor
Adjust fit and padding for a forced march
Recognize maintenance damage before it becomes failure
